transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-01
Time: 16:00 UTC / 09:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Lena (VenturePay Head of Security), Marcus (Platform Eng), Ravi (CTO), Ava (SRE), Oliver (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- VenturePay evaluating Redwood for payments-related ML features; primary concerns are compliance (SOC2/ISO), SSO integration, RBAC, audit logging retention, and encryption/KMS.
- Discussed differences between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments; trade-offs on latency vs cost vs data residency.
- Next steps: provide SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML integration guide, schedule deeper technical session and run benchmarks.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone thanks for joining. I think we have about 40 minutes today; quick intros, then we'll focus on security posture, what you need and where you are.
[00:12] Lena: Hi, Lena here. Head of Security at VenturePay, happy to be here. We just want to make sure any LLM infra we put in our payments path meets our controls.
[00:20] Marcus: Marcus, platform eng. We're responsible for infra and networking.
[00:24] Ravi: Ravi, CTO. Short on time but want to get the big picture.
[00:28] Ava: Ava, SRE — operational questions mostly.
[00:31] Oliver: Oliver, procurement — will chime on contracting/timelines.
[00:36] Samira: Samira from Redwood SE, hi all. I'll cover technical security and demo the SSO bits.
[00:41] Priya: Priya, solutions eng — I can follow up on dedicated/private architecture.
[00:46] Jared: Cool. Lena, want to kick off with your primary requirements?
[00:49] Lena: Sure, we have a checklist: SOC 2 type II or equivalent, ISO 27001 is nice to have, SSO with SAML and SCIM, RBAC, audit logs retention of at least 7 years for certain routes, encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), and strict data residency controls. Also need evidence of pen testing and ability to support audits.
[01:12] Samira: Got it. That's pretty standard — we frequently see all of these with finance customers. Redwood's offerings map to these: Hosted API is our managed public offering, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in an isolated tenancy, and Private is a customer-controlled plane (VPC/on-prem). For SOC2/ISO we have reports we share under NDA.
[01:32] Lena: When you say Dedicated, is it single-tenant network? Do we get private subnets and no commingling?
[01:39] Priya: In Dedicated we give reserved capacity for your tenant; network isolation is configurable — we can do dedicated VPC peering, private endpoints, and restrict egress. There's still a Redwood control plane unless you opt for Private where the control plane is customer-managed.
[01:53] Marcus: Ok and for Private, does that mean we host the inference VMs in our VPC and Redwood manages the software, or do we run everything ourselves?
[01:59] Priya: We offer a few Private models: (1) Customer-managed runtime where you deploy Redwood's inference runtime into your VPC/on-prem and we provide the orchestration package; (2) Fully air-gapped on-prem install where we hand over artifacts and you run it. In the partially managed model we integrate with your KMS — customer-managed keys.
[02:17] Ravi: How do you handle patching and security updates in the private on-prem scenario? We need SLAs for CVE remediation windows.
[02:23] Samira: For customer-managed Private installs we provide an update cadence and advisory feed; typical SLA for critical CVEs is within 72 hours for supported releases, plus backported patches if you're on our LTS channel. We can include a remediation SLA in enterprise contracts.
[02:36] Lena: You mentioned KMS — which KMS providers do you integrate with? We use AWS KMS and HashiCorp Vault in prod.
[02:43] Priya: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM integrations. HashiCorp Vault is supported via transit encryption patterns; we have docs and an integration guide. For Hosted customers we can offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key).
[02:59] Ava: For Hosted, if we use BYOK how do you prove keys aren't exfiltrated? Do you provide attestation or HSM logs?
[03:06] Samira: We use cloud KMS with audit trails; we can surface key usage logs. For high assurance we recommend Dedicated or Private with your KMS inside your VPC. We can also provide pen test reports and third-party attestations — again under NDA.
[03:20] Lena: Audit logs: we need immutable audit trails for admin actions and API access, and retention policy controls. Can you export logs to our SIEM?
[03:28] Samira: Absolutely — Redwood Console provides per-route and per-token logs; audit logs for control plane actions, role changes, and admin activity. You can forward logs via syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver or we can S3 dump for long-term retention. We also support WORM-like retention if you self-host the storage.
[03:45] Marcus: Any chance of log sampling or redaction? Payment data shouldn't be in plaintext in logs.
[03:50] Priya: We have configurable redaction hooks and automatic PII detection. For Hosted we recommend prefix/KV caching approaches to avoid storing raw payment data. You can also set policy to scrub request/response bodies before they hit persistent logs.
[04:03] Ravi: What about RBAC — we need at least role separation: admin, infra, SRE, auditor. Can RBAC integrate with our SSO groups?
[04:11] Samira: Yes, RBAC integrates with SAML/SCIM. We map SSO groups to roles; Redwood Console supports granular permissions (model deploy, rollout, view logs, billing). You can create audit-only roles. Changes to RBAC are logged.
[04:23] Lena: SAML flows — does Redwood support IdP-initiated login and SCIM provisioning? We use Okta.
[04:29] Samira: Yes to both. We have an Okta playbook; SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle and group sync. We can provide a test config to try in a sandbox.
[04:37] Oliver: On procurement/timing, we need to know which deployment mode is recommended for minimal friction vs max control. Our legal will want data residency and indemnities for hosted.
[04:46] Jared: For friction the Hosted API is fastest — you get API keys and start. For stronger controls and isolation, Dedicated is the middle ground (reservation and VPC options). Private gives you the most control but more setup. For a payments company, many customers start Hosted with strict contract terms and then move to Dedicated or Private as they prove the workload.
[05:03] Marcus: Any customers in fintech you can reference?
[05:06] Jared: We have a few finance customers — we can share references after an NDA.
[05:10] Lena: Data residency: we need EU data to stay in EU for certain PII; can you pin regions?
[05:16] Priya: Yes, you can pin model serving to regions and we can route based on policy. Dedicated pools can be placed in region-specific clusters. For Hosted we also support region pins for enterprise accounts.
[05:27] Ava: Performance question — for latency-sensitive inference in payments (sub-200ms p95), do you recommend hosting models on GPUs or CPU quantized variants?
[05:36] Samira: Typically GPU-backed Dedicated instances give best latency; for lower-cost but slightly higher latency we recommend quantized CPU variants with batching. We can run a benchmark with your sample prompts to give realistic numbers.
[05:46] Ravi: For regulatory audits, will you provide evidence like config snapshots, RBAC change history, and deployment manifests?
[05:53] Samira: Yes — we can export artifacts, signed logs, and configuration snapshots. We also keep deployment manifests for rollback and can provide change provenance.
[06:01] Lena: Pen testing — do you do continuous pen testing or annual? We need results of testing plus remediation timelines.
[06:07] Priya: We run annual third-party pen tests and internal vulnerability scanning more frequently. We can share summary findings and remediation plans under NDA.
[06:16] Marcus: How about network egress controls — can we restrict outbound to approved endpoints?
[06:20] Priya: For Dedicated and Private yes, you can lock egress and use NAT with tightly controlled rules. Hosted can restrict via private link or VPC peering options.
[06:29] Ava: Backups and retention — if we need 7 years for some logs, what storage pattern do you use and how do we ensure integrity?
[06:36] Samira: We can export logs to your long-term storage (S3 with versioning and WORM), or if you self-host you can keep immutable storage. We support hash-based integrity proofs and can provide periodic manifests.
[06:48] Lena: A few things I want in the artifact pack: SOC2 Type II, ISO attestation, pen test summary, SAML/SCIM guides, RBAC doc, KMS integration guide, sample log export pipeline. Also a data-flow diagram showing PII handling.
[07:02] Jared: We'll package that and send. We'll also include a sandbox account for you to test SSO/SCIM.
[07:09] Oliver: On contracting: can you provide pricing for a 3-month pilot on Hosted vs Dedicated pilot? We will compare TCO.
[07:16] Jared: Yes — we'll send a pilot pricing sheet and an example contract addendum for security requirements.
[07:22] Lena: One more: training and access reviews — can we schedule quarterly access reviews and quarterly security checkpoints?
[07:28] Samira: Absolutely, we have CSM offerings and can include quarterly security reviews in the engagement.
[07:33] Marcus: For the benchmark, what inputs do you need from us?
[07:36] Samira: Sample prompt set, traffic distribution (p95/p50), expected concurrency, and desired latency SLOs. We'll run it on Hosted/Dedicated and share numbers.
[07:46] Ravi: Sound plan. If we get the artifact pack and the benchmark we can decide next week.
[07:52] Jared: Great — recap, action items: we send SOC2/ISO and security artifacts, set up sandbox and SSO test, Samira runs benchmark once you send sample traffic, schedule technical deep-dive for Dedicated/Private options next week.
[08:06] Lena: Thank you.
[08:08] Oliver: Thanks everyone.
[08:10] Jared: End.
